'''Erode Subramanian Raja Gopal''' (12 May 1936 – 15 November 2018) was an Indian [[condensed matter physicist]], a former professor at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] and a former director of the [[National Physical Laboratory of India]]. Known for his research in [[condensed matter physics]], Raja Gopal was an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies – the [[Indian National Science Academy]], the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] – as well as a member of the [[Institute of Physics]]. He was a former [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] emeritus scientist, an alumnus of the [[University of Oxford]] and the author of three reference texts in [[condensed matter physics]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to Physical Sciences in 1978.

== Biography ==
[[File:University of Madras New.JPG|thumb|235px|left|University of Madras]]
[[File:Clarendon Laboratory, University of Oxford.jpg|thumb|Clarendon Laboratory]]
Born on 12 May 1936 at [[Salem, Tamil Nadu]],<ref name="curr_sci_obit">{{Cite journal |url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/115/11/2166.pdf |title=Personal News: Erode Subramanian Raja Gopal (1936-2018) |journal=[[Current Science]] |volume=115 |issue=11 |pages=2166–2167 |date=10 December 2018 }}</ref> E. S. Raja Gopal did his pre-graduate studies at [[St. Joseph's College, Tiruchirappalli]] and after earning a BSc (hons) from the [[University of Madras]],<ref name="Director's Address">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iiests.ac.in/images/all_pdf2/DirectorsAddress.pdf |title=Director's Address |date=4 March 2017 |publisher=Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421100117/http://www.iiests.ac.in/images/all_pdf2/DirectorsAddress.pdf |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> he continued at the university to complete an MA in physics in 1956 and a second master's degree by research (MSc) in 1958.<ref name="About the Speaker">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iisertvm.ac.in/colloquiums/read/71/1.phpx |title=About the Speaker |date=2017 |publisher=IISER, Thiruvananthapuram |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421094210/http://www.iisertvm.ac.in/colloquiums/read/71/1.phpx |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> Subsequently, he moved to the neighboring state of [[Karnataka]] to pursue his doctoral studies at the [[Indian Institute of Science]]<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Raja_Gopal,_Prof._Erode_Subramanian |title=Fellow profile |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421092113/http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Raja_Gopal,_Prof._Erode_Subramanian |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> and secured a PhD in 1961 under the guidance of distinguished experimental physicist [[R. S. Krishnan]].<ref name="curr_sci_obit"/><ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N81-0588 |title=Indian fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170424003552/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N81-0588 |archive-date=24 April 2017 }}</ref> He then undertook post-doctoral studies at the [[Clarendon Laboratory]] of the Department of Physics, [[University of Oxford]] under [[Kurt Mendelssohn]].<ref name="curr_sci_obit"/> Upon his return to India in 1964, he joined Indian Institute of Science (IISc) as a [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] pool officer at the department of physics, to commence an association which would last over 35 years. He held several positions at IISc during this period, where he became an assistant professor in 1965, a full professor in 1969 and the dean of the faculty of science in 1976. He chaired the department of physics during 1977–80 and Regional Sophisticated Instrumentation Centre (present-day NMR Research Centre) from 1983 to 1989.<ref name="Director's Address" />

In 1991, Raja Gopal was appointed the director of [[National Physical Laboratory of India]] (NPL) but he continued his association with IISc as the MSIL chair professor from 1991 to 1994.<ref name="MSIL chair professor">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iisc.ac.in/about/endowed-chairs/endowed-chairs-for-the-faculty/ |title=MSIL chair professor |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170513003017/http://www.iisc.ac.in/about/endowed-chairs/endowed-chairs-for-the-faculty/ |archive-date=13 May 2017 }}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|MSIL Chair professorship is an endowment from Mysore Sales International Limited, a [[Government of Karnataka]] undertaking}} He headed NPL till his retirement from official service in 1997 after which he remained with the laboratory as a CSIR emeritus scientist for a while before returning to Bengaluru to rejoin IISc holding the CSIR position<ref name="About the Speaker" /> and became an emeritus professor of the department of physics, a position he held until his death.<ref name="E.S. Raja Gopal Emeritus Professor">{{Cite web |url=http://www.physics.iisc.ernet.in/people-faculty.php |title=E.S. Raja Gopal Emeritus Professor |date=2017 |publisher=Department of Physics, IISc |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130622204619/http://www.physics.iisc.ernet.in/people-faculty.php |archive-date=22 June 2013 }}</ref> At IISc, he held the position of a senior scientist of the Indian National Science Academy from 2001 to 2006 and was an honorary scientist of INSA since then.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

Raja Gopal, who was a resident of [[Malleswaram]] in Bengaluru,<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=R |title=NASI fellows |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315130140/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=R |archive-date=15 March 2016 }}</ref> died on 15 November 2018.<ref name="Fellowship - Indian Academy of Sciences">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Raja_Gopal,_Prof._Erode_Subramanian |title=Fellowship - Indian Academy of Sciences |date=17 November 2018 |website=www.ias.ac.in |language=en |access-date=17 November 2018}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
[[File:Argon ice 1.jpg|thumb|right|[[Phase transition]] of [[Argon|Argon ice]] – transitions from solid to liquid to gas]]
Raja Gopal has worked on various aspects of condensed matter physics especially [[Critical point (thermodynamics)|critical point]] phenomena which assisted in understanding the [[Law of the Rectilinear Diameter]] and its breakdown.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=248 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421093948/http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=248 |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> He studied [[electrical resistivity]] in relation to non-equilibrium critical point phenomena and elucidated its unusual behavior.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web |url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |date=1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 |access-date=20 April 2017 }}</ref> His studies of the ''liquid systems and [[Order and disorder|disordered]] materials'' with regard to their [[phase transitions]] returned precision measurements which helped in observing ''particle-hole asymmetry in the liquid-gas critical phenomena in binary liquid mixtures'' for the first time.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> [[Percolation threshold]] in covalently bonded [[chalcogenide glass]]es through precise measurements was another of his notable findings. He has published his research findings by way of over 250 articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} of which 167 have been listed in the article repository of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Raja_Gopal=3AErode_Subramanian=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421092514/http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Raja_Gopal=3AErode_Subramanian=3A=3A.html |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> He has also written three books: ''High Temperature Superconductors'',<ref name="SubramanyamGopal1989">{{cite book |author1=S. V. Subramanyam |author2=Erode Subramanian Raja Gopal |title=High temperature superconductors |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uxyaAAAAIAAJ |date=1 August 1989 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-470-21396-4 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421111235/https://books.google.com/books?id=uxyaAAAAIAAJ |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> ''Specific Heats at Low Temperatures'',<ref name="Gopal1966">{{cite book |author=Erode Subramanian Raja Gopal |title=Specific heats at low temperatures |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jAhRAAAAMAAJ |year=1966 |publisher=Plenum Press |isbn=9780608057583 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421094824/https://books.google.com/books?id=jAhRAAAAMAAJ |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> and ''Statistical Mechanics and Properties of Matter: Theory and Applications''<ref name="Gopal1974">{{cite book |author=Erode Subramanian Raja Gopal |title=Statistical Mechanics and Properties of Matter: Theory and Applications |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BhZjAgAACAAJ |year=1974 |publisher=Ellis Horwood |isbn=978-0-85312-054-4 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421111330/https://books.google.com/books?id=BhZjAgAACAAJ |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> and has supervised the studies of over 60 master's and doctoral scholars.<ref name="About the Speaker" />

== Awards and honors ==
The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded Raja Gopal the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1978.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409021146/http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |archive-date=9 April 2017 }}</ref> When the Acoustical Society of India (ASI) instituted an annual award for articles published in its official journal in 1980, an article co-written by Raja Gopal, ''Ultrasonic study of chromatin and DNA solution at High Pressure up to 3 kbar'', earned the inaugural Sir C.V. Raman Award;<ref name="Sir C.V. Raman Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.acousticsindia.org/5_5_awards.html |title=Sir C.V. Raman Award |date=2017 |publisher=Acoustical Society of India |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421100336/http://www.acousticsindia.org/5_5_awards.html |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> ASI would honor him again with the 1993–94 Dr. S Bhagavantam Award for ''contributions in the field of Acoustics''.<ref name="Dr. S Bhagavantam Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.acousticsindia.org/5_1_awards.html |title=Dr. S Bhagavantam Award |date=2017 |publisher=Acoustical Society of India |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421100217/http://www.acousticsindia.org/5_1_awards.html |archive-date=21 April 2017 }}</ref> In between, he received the Inventions Promotions Award of the [[National Research Development Corporation]] (NRDC) in 1984.<ref name="Director's Address" /> He received the Homi Jehangir Bhabha Medal of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 1993<ref name="Homi Jehangir Bhabha Medal ">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34 |title=Homi Jehangir Bhabha Medal |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34 |archive-date=16 September 2016 }}</ref> and the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Biotech Research Society of India in 2004.<ref name="BRSI Lifetime Achievement Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.brsi.in/awards/ |title=BRSI Lifetime Achievement Award |date=2017 |publisher=Biotech Research Society of India |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829234114/http://www.brsi.in/awards |archive-date=29 August 2017 }}</ref> He was also a recipient of the 2005 Lifetime Achievement Award of the Instrument Society of India<ref name="ISOI Lifetime Achievement Award">{{Cite web |url=http://isu.iisc.ernet.in/~isoi/Awards.html |title=ISOI Lifetime Achievement Award |date=2017 |publisher=Instrument Society of India |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150512203121/http://isu.iisc.ernet.in/~isoi/Awards.html |archive-date=12 May 2015 }}</ref> and his alma mater, Indian Institute of Science, honored him with Distinguished Alumnus Award in 2008.<ref name="Distinguished Alumni conferred Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iiscalumni.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/IIScAA-newsletter-issue1_March-2009.pdf |title=Distinguished Alumni conferred Awards |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170422032846/http://www.iiscalumni.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/IIScAA-newsletter-issue1_March-2009.pdf |archive-date=22 April 2017 }}</ref>

|publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016
